content: {"rule":"K-C","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text resolves Matthew 1:16 against the defender's cited Luke and Numbers texts by asking whether any text's own words state the contrary, which is the chain-collision situation rule K-C governs.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D1 vs C3 (Matthew 1:16): UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē states no verdict on the begetter in either direction, and the defender answered Luke 1:27, Luke 2:4 and Numbers 1:2 in [CR2] section A.3 and [CR3]; the verb change is real [L1]/[L2] but neither text's own words state the other reading's contrary.","rule_words":"When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.","room":"When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together: (1) this triggers chain-against-chain footing and bars the stating-verse test, or (2) the rule does not apply unless the pressed witnesses are the pressing side's own chain.","why":"The judge finds the link underdetermined because no text's own words state the contrary, which is the retired verse-by-verse stating-verse test rather than chain-against-chain footing."}
